title: The Stock Market Crash of 1929
text: The Wall Street Crash of 1929, beginning on October 24 (Black Thursday) and culminating on October 29 (Black Tuesday), was the most devastating stock market crash in U.S. history. The crash marked the beginning of the Great Depression, a decade-long economic crisis that affected all Western industrialized countries. Stock prices fell by approximately 25% in the two days of Black Thursday and Black Tuesday. By 1932, the Dow Jones Industrial Average had lost 89% of its value from its 1929 peak. The crash was preceded by a speculative bubble fueled by buying on margin (borrowed money). It led to widespread bank failures and unemployment that reached 25% in the United States by 1933.
